summary: Tested new Weight PDF export feature (dragon-weight.tsx + weightPdf.ts) and regression-checked existing weight tracking + admin JSON export. Export button placement/UI confirmed correct. No-data guard toast confirmed. Web-platform-unsupported graceful toast confirmed (verified with temporary weight entries added to logan, then cleaned up). Full weight regression (add entry, chart render at 2+ entries, history list, delete, close button) all working with no breakage from the new feature. Code review of weightPdf.ts HTML/SVG generation found no structural issues. However found a PRE-EXISTING (not caused by this session's dialogTitle-only change) bug in Admin > Database > Export: it throws an ungraceful error toast 'this.validatePath is not a function' on web instead of a clean fallback message, unlike the new weight PDF export which correctly Platform.OS==='web' short-circuits.

ui_bugs.issue: On web, 'Export database' button throws raw JS error toast 'this.validatePath is not a function' (root cause: expo-file-system's `File`/`Paths` API - used to write the JSON backup - is not supported on web, confirmed via console log 'expo-file-system is not supported on web'; Paths.document is likely undefined on web causing the crash). This is a pre-existing issue (git diff shows only the dialogTitle string was added this session, the File/Paths write logic is untouched), but it is NOT a graceful fallback like the new weight PDF export achieves via an explicit Platform.OS==='web' check. Recommend adding a similar web-platform guard/graceful toast to handleExport for consistency.

action_items: Consider adding a Platform.OS==='web' guard (or try/catch with a user-friendly message) to admin.tsx handleExport, mirroring the pattern already used in dragon-weight.tsx handleExportPdf, so web users see a clean fallback message instead of 'this.validatePath is not a function'.

This is not a regression from the reviewed session's dialogTitle change (confirmed via git diff of admin.tsx - only the dialogTitle key/value was added), but should be fixed for consistency with the new PDF feature's UX.
critical_code_review_comments: weightPdf.ts: buildWeightChartSvg and buildWeightPdfHtml look structurally sound - escapeHtml() correctly applied to dragonName and entry.note (user-controlled fields) preventing malformed/injected HTML; table/chart only rendered when entries exist (guarded by sortedAsc.length checks) avoiding NaN/empty-array edge cases (Math.min/max on empty array would be Infinity/-Infinity but this path is guarded by length>=2 check before calling the chart function, and length>0 before building rows).
computeExactAge handles same-day/near-birthday edge cases (month rollover, day-of-month comparison) correctly for typical age ranges seen in the app (dragons with birthdays in the past).

dragon-weight.tsx handleExportPdf: correctly guards on entries.length===0 first, then Platform.OS==='web' second - matches the required order per the review request. Loading state (exportingPdf) properly disables the button and shows ActivityIndicator, preventing double-taps.
No exposed MongoDB _id or hardcoded URLs observed in the reviewed files; api calls use the shared api util.

All testable web-platform paths (no-data guard, web-unsupported message, button placement, regression of add/chart/history/delete/close) passed. The admin export bug found is pre-existing and unrelated to this session's change; flagged for main agent's awareness but does not block this feature's sign-off.
rca_of_issue: Admin 'Export database' web crash: handleExport() uses `new File(Paths.document, fileName)` from expo-file-system (new File System API), which per console log is 'not supported on web'. On web, Paths.document is likely undefined/null, so `new File(undefined, fileName)` produces a File object whose internal validatePath method is missing/undefined, throwing 'this.validatePath is not a function' when .write() is called. Confirmed via git diff that only the dialogTitle string in Sharing.shareAsync was added this session - the File/Paths logic causing the crash predates this session and is unrelated to the reviewed weight-PDF feature.
